scanners.disabled_reason: Offered the entire DriverStore FileRepository (7.13 GB here) as one deletable item. Tagged danger so it was never auto-selected, but ticking it costs the machine its drivers. Reclaiming space here means removing SUPERSEDED driver packages one at a time - pnputil /enum-drivers then /delete-driver oemN.inf - which is a different feature, not a directory delete. Kept as data so the knowledge does not have to be rediscovered.

scanners.label: Installer payload cache (Visual Studio, .NET, redistributables)
scanners.description: Setup payloads kept by Visual Studio, .NET and the VC++ redistributables so they can repair or modify themselves without the original download. Routinely several GB on a dev machine and covered by nothing before this. Caution, not safe: removing it means the next repair re-downloads. No age floor, deliberately: min_age_default tests the DIRECTORY's own mtime, so any recent write inside hides the whole folder from the report. Safety level is what conveys the caution here.

scanners.label: CHKDSK recovered fragments (FOUND.*) on every fixed drive
scanners.description: Orphaned clusters CHKDSK recovered into FOUND.000 and never cleaned up. Almost always junk, occasionally the only copy of something - hence caution, not safe.

scanners.label: Recycle Bin on every fixed drive
scanners.description: Deleted files still occupying space, per volume. Replaces the two hand-written scanners that did this - scan_recycle_bin and scan_recycle_bin_drive were byte-identical duplicates, so the same bytes were reported under two names.

scanners.label: Temp folders on every fixed drive
scanners.description: A \temp or \tmp folder at the root of any fixed drive. Every other temp scanner is %TEMP% or %windir%\Temp, both on C:; E:\temp held 20.36 GB on the machine this was written for, which nothing in the cleaner could find. Caution rather than safe: a drive-root temp folder is one somebody made on purpose, unlike %TEMP%, and the age floor keeps today's files out of it. No age floor, deliberately: min_age_default tests the DIRECTORY's own mtime, so any recent write inside hides the whole folder from the report. Safety level is what conveys the caution here.
